title: Judges 13 — The messenger of YHWH and the birth of Shimshon (Samson)

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

verdicts.reasoning: wayyōsip̄û ... laʿăśôṯ hāraʿ ... ʾarbāʿîm šānâ: 'again did' renders the auxiliary ysp. Exact.
ʾîš ʾeḥāḏ miṣṣorʿâ mimmišpaḥaṯ haddānî ... wəʾištô ʿăqārâ wəlōʾ yālāḏâ: exact; the Alter type-scene citation is apt.

wəhārîṯ wəyālaḏt bēn: perfects consecutive, future 'but you shall conceive and bear a son'. The reception note accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 (unions between creators and women; barrenness removed) and the line renders only the announcement.
hiššāmrî nāʾ wəʾal-tištî yayin wəšēḵār wəʾal-tōʾḵlî kol-ṭāmēʾ: exact (note's 'anything unclean' vs line 'nothing unclean' is the same sense).

Re-parsed: kî hinnāḵ hārâ wəyōlaḏt bēn ûmôrâ lōʾ-yaʿăleh ʿal-rōʾšô kî-nəzîr ʾĕlōhîm yihyeh hannaʿar min-habbāṭen. The future reading of hārâ after v 3 is the majority construal (ASV, NRSV, NJPS 'you are going to conceive'), and the present alternative is recorded; 'a Nazirite to Elohim' keeps the anarthrous genitive (clause 2). The rationale openly notes that the tense choice bears on the canon's reading of v 9, which keeps the decision auditable. Reception note confined to apparatus.

ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm bāʾ ʾēlay ... kəmarʾēh malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm nôrāʾ məʾōḏ: articular title rendered 'The man of the Elohim' (ratified ish-ha-elohim rule; ASV indefinite recorded). wəʾeṯ-šəmô lōʾ-higgîḏ lî. Exact.
Repetition with ʿaḏ-yôm môṯô and without the razor clause, both noted. Exact.
wayyeʿtar mānôaḥ ... bî ʾăḏônāy (plene, divine vocalization, re-checked in the source) 'Oh, Lord'; hannaʿar hayyûllāḏ 'the boy who is to be born'. Exact.

wayyišmaʿ hāʾĕlōhîm ... wayyāḇōʾ malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm ʿôḏ ... ûmānôaḥ ʾîšāh ʾên ʿimmāh: literal; both articular forms kept. The reception note fairly reports TBWTT ch. 3 and states that the Hebrew narrates only the coming and the absence.
wattəmahēr ... wattāroṣ ... hāʾîš ʾăšer-bāʾ bayyôm ʾēlāy 'the other day' (ASV). Exact.
hăʾattâ hāʾîš ʾăšer-dibbartā ʾel-hāʾiššâ wayyōʾmer ʾānî: exact.

ʿattâ yāḇōʾ ḏəḇāreyḵā ... mišpaṭ-hannaʿar ûmaʿăśēhû. Defensible. Non-blocking: the note glosses maʿăśeh as the boy's 'conduct or task', while the line has 'what shall be done for him'; align them (either line 'and what shall be his work?' or a note that says the line takes maʿăśēhû as what is to be done for him).
mikkōl ʾăšer-ʾāmartî ʾel-hāʾiššâ tiššāmēr: 'let her beware' (3fs jussive sense). Exact.
mikkōl ʾăšer-yēṣēʾ miggep̄en hayyayin ... kōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwîṯîhā tišmōr: exact.
naʿṣərâ-nnāʾ ʾôṯāḵ wənaʿăśeh ləp̄āneyḵā gəḏî ʿizzîm: exact.
ʾim-taʿṣərēnî lōʾ-ʾōḵal bəlaḥmeḵā ... ʿōlâ laYHWH taʿălennâ: concessive 'Though you detain me'. Exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv dbryk 'your words' / Qere dəḇārəḵā 'your word': Qere translated, ASV Ketiv recorded. mî šəmeḵā 'What is your name' with the literal 'Who' in the note. Exact.
lāmmâ zeh tišʾal lišmî wəhûʾ-p̄eliʾ: 'seeing it is wonderful' (ASV); the refusal is not turned into a name. Correct.

wayyaʿal ʿal-haṣṣûr laYHWH ûmap̄liʾ laʿăśôṯ: subject of the participle left unexpressed against the ASV '[the angel]'; LXX 'to the Lord who works wonders' accurately reported. Correct under the MT-baseline rule.

baʿălôṯ hallahaḇ mēʿal hammizbēaḥ haššāmaymâ wayyaʿal malʾaḵ-YHWH bəlahaḇ hammizbēaḥ: the directional šāmaymâ belongs to the flame, so 'toward the skies' fits the physical-register test; 'went up' keeps the single verb ʿlh. Comment for the founder only: this is the closest analogue to Eliyahu's ascent, which the founder ratified as 'to the heavens' (2 Kgs 2:1, 11); the Editor's distinction (flame's direction, not the messenger's destination) is grammatically sound.
wəlōʾ-yāsap̄ ʿôḏ ... ləhērāʾōh ... ʾāz yāḏaʿ mānôaḥ: exact.

môṯ nāmûṯ kî ʾĕlōhîm rāʾînû: anarthrous object in direct speech, 'we have seen Elohim' under clause 2 and genesis-woh Gen 32:31; the note gives NJPS 'a divine being' and the contextual referent. Defensible.
lû ḥāp̄ēṣ ... lōʾ-lāqaḥ ... wəlōʾ herʾānû ... wəḵāʿēṯ lōʾ hišmîʿānû kāzōʾṯ: unreal conditional rendered correctly. Exact.
wattiqrāʾ ʾeṯ-šəmô šimšôn ... wayḇārăḵēhû YHWH: exact.
wattāḥel rûaḥ YHWH ləp̄aʿămô: 'began to move him' (ASV verb kept; pāʿam 'impel'); 'the ruach of YHWH' per the ratified transliteration. Exact.

After reading it, no verdict changed. The report confirms it did not check the shofar Exodus refIds (the reviewer did: EXO-WOH-20:15, not 20:18) and names the ark collision risk (the reviewer checked exodus-woh chapter-25 and the Torah diff: no ʾărôn entry exists there; six Ex 25 refIds should join the central entry). The report's note that the Torah diff touches no entry this diff modifies is contradicted by the data (hishtachavah), which strengthens the revise on that op. founderDecisionRecommendations.1-1Sam-6:18-great-stone: Ship. ʾāḇēl cannot be construed (two failed agreements, contradiction with vv 14-15); ʾeḇen with LXX, Targum and some Hebrew MSS is the standard correction (Driver 1913; McCarter 1980). Ratify the exception exactly as narrowly worded (MT grammatically impossible + Hebrew-manuscript reading supported by the versions).
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-gentilics: Keep the Kings '-ite' rule in the Former Prophets now (option c); it maps one-to-one to the ASV and is already ratified for Kings. For the later corpus pass, the reviewer prefers (a) '-ite' throughout, with the central pelishtim-caphtor plural becoming 'the Pelishtites', because 'the Pelishtite' beside 'the Pelishtim' is the one jarring pair. No philological issue either way; it is a presentation choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-Judg-6:40-the-Elohim: Confirm. The ratified Kings text explicitly leaves the central narrative-subject rule ('the Elohim') in force and limits the article-less form to predicates, genitives and direct-speech subjects; the brief's paraphrase was inaccurate. Clause 6 applies the ratified text exactly.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-Judg-6:34-clothed: Ship. lāḇəšâ is literally 'clothed' (BDB; same idiom 1 Chr 12:19; 2 Chr 24:20; Block), and keeping Judges' four verbs distinct is a gain in accuracy.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-herem: Ship. 'devote(d) to destruction' is the standard modern rendering (NRSV; HALOT) and the only consistent one; it makes the Josh 6 / Josh 10 connection visible without moral editorializing.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-shofar-promotion: Approve the promotion after the refId fix (EXO-WOH-20:15 for 20:18; optionally add EXO-WOH-19:13). Retire the 1-kings-woh shofar entry to a pointer and let the exodus-woh overlays cite the central id.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּסִ֙פוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְּנֵ֧ם יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el again did what was evil in the sight of YHWH; and YHWH gave them into the hand of the Pelishtim forty years.

notes.official: The framework formula (cf. 6:1); *ʾarbāʿîm šānâ* 'forty years', the longest oppression in the book. Pelishtim = Philistines (central `pelishtim-caphtor`) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֧ד מִצָּרְעָ֛ה מִמִּשְׁפַּ֥חַת הַדָּנִ֖י וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מָנ֑וֹחַ וְאִשְׁתּ֥וֹ עֲקָרָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יָלָֽדָה׃

i18n.en: And there was a certain man of Tzor'ah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoach; and his wife was barren and had not borne.

notes.official: Tzor'ah = Zorah; *mimmišpaḥaṯ haddānî* 'of the clan of the Danites' (collective gentilic); Manoach = Manoah (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *wəʾištô ʿăqārâ wəlōʾ yālāḏâ* 'and his wife was barren and had not borne' (`sarai-aqarah`): the type-scene of the barren wife and the announced son (Gen 16:11; 18:10-14; 25:21; 1 Sam 1) (Alter, *The Art of Biblical Narrative*, 1981). The woman is never named.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּרָ֥א מַלְאַךְ־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֗יהָ הִנֵּה־נָ֤א אַתְּ־עֲקָרָה֙ וְלֹ֣א יָלַ֔דְתְּ וְהָרִ֖ית וְיָלַ֥דְתְּ בֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH appeared to the woman and said to her, "Behold now, you are barren and have not borne; but you shall conceive and bear a son.

notes.official:
*wayyērāʾ malʾaḵ-YHWH ʾel-hāʾiššâ* 'And the messenger of YHWH appeared to the woman' (`malakh-yhwh-messenger`). *wəhārîṯ wəyālaḏt bēn* 'but you shall conceive and bear a son': perfects with *waw* consecutive, future after 'you are barren' (`harah-you-shall-conceive-judges-13`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse and reads Judg 13 as a further case of union between the creators and human women, the woman's barrenness being removed so that she would know her child was exceptional. The line renders the announcement as the Hebrew gives it and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הִשָּׁ֣מְרִי נָ֔א וְאַל־תִּשְׁתִּ֖י יַ֣יִן וְשֵׁכָ֑ר וְאַל־תֹּאכְלִ֖י כָּל־טָמֵֽא׃

i18n.en: Now therefore beware, I pray you, and drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean.

notes.official: *wəʿattâ hiššāmrî nāʾ* 'Now therefore beware, I pray you'. *yayin wəšēḵār* 'wine or strong drink' (ASV): *šēḵār* is fermented drink other than wine. *kol-ṭāmēʾ* 'anything unclean'. The mother keeps the Nazirite abstentions of Num 6:3-4 during the pregnancy (`nezir-elohim-nazirite-to-elohim-judges-13`).

paragraphs.text: כִּי֩ הִנָּ֨ךְ הָרָ֜ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֗ן וּמוֹרָה֙ לֹא־יַעֲלֶ֣ה עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ כִּֽי־נְזִ֧יר אֱלֹהִ֛ים יִהְיֶ֥ה הַנַּ֖עַר מִן־הַבָּ֑טֶן וְה֗וּא יָחֵ֛ל לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

i18n.en: For behold, you shall conceive and bear a son; and no razor shall come upon his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to Elohim from the womb; and he shall begin to save Yisra'el from the hand of the Pelishtim."

notes.official:
*kî hinnāḵ hārâ wəyōlaḏt bēn* 'For behold, you shall conceive and bear a son': *hārâ* is the adjective 'pregnant', which after *hinnēh* can be present ('you are pregnant', as at Gen 16:11) or imminent future. After v 3 the line keeps the future, with the ASV and NRSV (NJPS 'you are going to conceive') (`harah-you-shall-conceive-judges-13`). *ûmôrâ lōʾ-yaʿăleh ʿal-rōʾšô* 'and no razor shall come upon his head' (Num 6:5; cf. 1 Sam 1:11). *kî-nəzîr ʾĕlōhîm yihyeh hannaʿar min-habbāṭen* 'for the boy shall be a Nazirite to Elohim from the womb' (ASV 'a Nazirite unto God'): *nāzîr* 'one set apart', the status of Num 6:1-21, here lifelong and imposed before birth (`nezir-elohim-nazirite-to-elohim-judges-13`); *ʾĕlōhîm* is an anarthrous genitive, without article (clause 2 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). *wəhûʾ yāḥēl ləhôšîaʿ* 'and he shall begin to save': only begin, since the Pelishtim remain until David.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 4-5 ('a Nazarite unto God from the womb') and reads Shimshon's uncut hair as natural antennas for telepathic contact with the creators, whose loss explains the loss of his 'strength' in Judg 16. The line renders *môrâ*, *rōʾš* and *nəzîr ʾĕlōhîm* literally and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֣א הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לְאִישָׁהּ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִ֤ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֙ בָּ֣א אֵלַ֔י וּמַרְאֵ֕הוּ כְּמַרְאֵ֛ה מַלְאַ֥ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים נוֹרָ֣א מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֤א שְׁאִלְתִּ֙יהוּ֙ אֵֽי־מִזֶּ֣ה ה֔וּא וְאֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לֹֽא־הִגִּ֥יד לִֽי׃

i18n.en: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, "The man of the Elohim came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the messenger of the Elohim, very fearsome; and I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

notes.official: *ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm bāʾ ʾēlay* 'The man of the Elohim came to me' (ASV 'A man of God'): the title is articular and is rendered under `ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-former-prophets`; the article on the genitive makes the chain definite. It is the prophetic title of Kings, and the woman uses it before she knows what the visitor is. *ûmarʾēhû kəmarʾēh malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm nôrāʾ məʾōḏ* 'and his appearance was like the appearance of the messenger of the Elohim, very fearsome' (ASV 'very terrible'; `malakh-elohim-messenger`; clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`). *wəʾeṯ-šəmô lōʾ-higgîḏ lî* 'and he did not tell me his name' anticipates v 18.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י הִנָּ֥ךְ הָרָ֖ה וְיֹלַ֣דְתְּ בֵּ֑ן וְעַתָּ֞ה אַל־תִּשְׁתִּ֣י ׀ יַ֣יִן וְשֵׁכָ֗ר וְאַל־תֹּֽאכְלִי֙ כָּל־טֻמְאָ֔ה כִּֽי־נְזִ֤יר אֱלֹהִים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַנַּ֔עַר מִן־הַבֶּ֖טֶן עַד־י֥וֹם מוֹתֽוֹ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: But he said to me, 'Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son; and now drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to Elohim from the womb to the day of his death.'"

notes.official: She repeats the announcement and adds *ʿaḏ-yôm môṯô* 'to the day of his death', which foreshadows 16:30; she does not mention the razor (`nezir-elohim-nazirite-to-elohim-judges-13`; `harah-you-shall-conceive-judges-13`). 'a Nazirite to Elohim' (clause 2 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּעְתַּ֥ר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בִּ֣י אֲדוֹנָ֔י אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֞ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֗חְתָּ יָבוֹא־נָ֥א עוֹד֙ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ וְיוֹרֵ֕נוּ מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַנַּ֥עַר הַיּוּלָּֽד׃

i18n.en: Then Manoach entreated YHWH and said, "Oh, Lord, let the man of the Elohim whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we shall do for the boy who is to be born."

notes.official: *wayyeʿtar mānôaḥ ʾel-YHWH* 'Then Manoach entreated YHWH' (`atar-l-yhwh-intercession`). *bî ʾăḏônāy* 'Oh, Lord' (divine vocalization, as 6:15). *ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the man of the Elohim' (articular; `ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-former-prophets`; clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּק֣וֹל מָנ֑וֹחַ וַיָּבֹ֣א מַלְאַךְ֩ הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים ע֜וֹד אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וְהִיא֙ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וּמָנ֥וֹחַ אִישָׁ֖הּ אֵ֥ין עִמָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And the Elohim listened to the voice of Manoach; and the messenger of the Elohim came again to the woman as she was sitting in the field; but Manoach her husband was not with her.

notes.official:
*wayyišmaʿ hāʾĕlōhîm* 'And the Elohim listened' and *malʾaḵ hāʾĕlōhîm* 'the messenger of the Elohim' (both articular, clause 1 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`; `malakh-elohim-messenger`). *ûmānôaḥ ʾîšāh ʾên ʿimmāh* 'but Manoach her husband was not with her': the second visit answers Manoach's prayer but comes to the woman, who then fetches her husband (v 10).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse and reads the husband's absence as the occasion of the conception of Shimshon by one of the creators. The Hebrew narrates only the messenger's coming and the husband's absence, and the line renders it literally; the reading belongs to the canon's interpretation, not to the translation.

paragraphs.text: וַתְּמַהֵר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתָּ֖רָץ וַתַּגֵּ֣ד לְאִישָׁ֑הּ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֨ה נִרְאָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א בַיּ֖וֹם אֵלָֽי׃

i18n.en: And the woman hurried and ran and told her husband, and said to him, "Behold, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me."

notes.official: *bayyôm* 'the other day' (ASV), literally 'on the day', i.e. earlier.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֛קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מָנ֖וֹחַ אַחֲרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־הָאִ֔ישׁ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הַאַתָּ֥ה הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֥רְתָּ אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And Manoach arose and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I am."

notes.official: *hăʾattâ hāʾîš ʾăšer-dibbartā ʾel-hāʾiššâ* 'Are you the man who spoke to the woman?' *wayyōʾmer ʾānî* 'And he said, I am.'

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מָנ֔וֹחַ עַתָּ֖ה יָבֹ֣א דְבָרֶ֑יךָ מַה־יִּֽהְיֶ֥ה מִשְׁפַּט־הַנַּ֖עַר וּמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

i18n.en: And Manoach said, "Now let your words come to pass. What shall be the ordering of the boy, and what shall be done for him?"

notes.official: *ʿattâ yāḇōʾ ḏəḇāreyḵā* 'Now let your words come to pass' (ASV), a wish; it can also be read as a temporal clause ('When your words come true', NJPS). *mišpaṭ-hannaʿar ûmaʿăśēhû* 'the ordering of the boy, and what shall be done for him' (ASV): *mišpāṭ* is the rule or regimen (NJPS 'rules'); *maʿăśēhû*, literally 'his doing', is rendered with the ASV as 'what shall be done for him', and can also mean his conduct or task.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מָנ֑וֹחַ מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֶל־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה תִּשָּׁמֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH said to Manoach, "Of all that I said to the woman let her beware.

notes.official: *mikkōl ʾăšer-ʾāmartî ʾel-hāʾiššâ tiššāmēr* 'Of all that I said to the woman let her beware': the messenger repeats only the mother's obligations (`malakh-yhwh-messenger`).

paragraphs.text: מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא֩ מִגֶּ֨פֶן הַיַּ֜יִן לֹ֣א תֹאכַ֗ל וְיַ֤יִן וְשֵׁכָר֙ אַל־תֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וְכָל־טֻמְאָ֖ה אַל־תֹּאכַ֑ל כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּיתִ֖יהָ תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: She shall not eat of anything that comes from the vine, nor drink wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean; all that I commanded her let her keep."

notes.official: *mikkōl ʾăšer-yēṣēʾ miggep̄en hayyayin* 'of anything that comes from the vine', the wording of Num 6:4 (`nezir-elohim-nazirite-to-elohim-judges-13`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מָנ֖וֹחַ אֶל־מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה נַעְצְרָה־נָּ֣א אוֹתָ֔ךְ וְנַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְפָנֶ֖יךָ גְּדִ֥י עִזִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And Manoach said to the messenger of YHWH, "Let us detain you, I pray you, and let us prepare a kid of the goats for you."

notes.official: *naʿṣərâ-nnāʾ ʾôṯāḵ* 'Let us detain you, I pray you': the offer of hospitality of Gen 18:5 and Judg 6:18-19.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מָנ֗וֹחַ אִם־תַּעְצְרֵ֙נִי֙ לֹא־אֹכַ֣ל בְּלַחְמֶ֔ךָ וְאִם־תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה עֹלָ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה תַּעֲלֶ֑נָּה כִּ֚י לֹא־יָדַ֣ע מָנ֔וֹחַ כִּֽי־מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH said to Manoach, "Though you detain me, I will not eat of your bread; but if you will prepare a burnt-offering, offer it to YHWH." For Manoach did not know that he was the messenger of YHWH.

notes.official: *lōʾ-ʾōḵal bəlaḥmeḵā* 'I will not eat of your bread'. *kî lōʾ-yāḏaʿ mānôaḥ kî-malʾaḵ YHWH hûʾ* 'For Manoach did not know that he was the messenger of YHWH': the narrator's aside explains why food was offered. *ʿōlâ* 'a burnt-offering' (`olah-burnt-offering`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל־מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה מִ֣י שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־יָבֹ֥א דבריך [דְבָרְךָ֖] וְכִבַּדְנֽוּךָ׃

i18n.en: And Manoach said to the messenger of YHWH, "What is your name, that when your word comes to pass we may honor you?"

notes.official: *mî šəmeḵā* 'What is your name', literally 'Who is your name'. *kî-yāḇōʾ ḏəḇārəḵā* 'when your word comes to pass' translates the Qere (singular); the Ketiv *dbryk* 'your words', which the ASV follows ('thy words'), agrees with v 12 (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-former-prophets`). *wəḵibbaḏnûḵā* 'we may honor you', perhaps with a gift.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לּוֹ֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה תִּשְׁאַ֣ל לִשְׁמִ֑י וְהוּא־פֶ֛לִאי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH said to him, "Why is it that you ask after my name, seeing it is wonderful?"

notes.official: *lāmmâ zeh tišʾal lišmî* 'Why is it that you ask after my name' (`name-refusal-formula`; Gen 32:30). *wəhûʾ-p̄eliʾ* 'seeing it is wonderful' (ASV): the adjective, written *plʾy*, means 'wonderful, beyond comprehension' (BDB; Ps 139:6 'too wonderful for me'; cf. Isa 9:5 *peleʾ*); NRSV 'it is too wonderful', NJPS 'it is unknowable'. The root *plʾ* links the refusal with v 19 *map̄liʾ laʿăśôṯ* 'did wondrously' and with Gid'on's 'wonders' (6:13). The answer refuses a name and is not transliterated as one (`peli-wonderful-name-judges-13-18`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מָנ֜וֹחַ אֶת־גְּדִ֤י הָעִזִּים֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַל עַל־הַצּ֖וּר לַֽיהוָ֑ה וּמַפְלִ֣א לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת וּמָנ֥וֹחַ וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ רֹאִֽים׃

i18n.en: So Manoach took the kid of the goats with the meal-offering, and offered it up on the rock to YHWH; and he did wondrously, while Manoach and his wife looked on.

notes.official: *wayyaʿal ʿal-haṣṣûr laYHWH* 'and offered it up on the rock to YHWH' (*ṣûr*, as 6:21; `mishenet-staff-fire-from-the-rock-judges-6-21`); *hamminḥâ* 'the meal-offering' (`qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`). *ûmap̄liʾ laʿăśôṯ* 'and he did wondrously': the participle has no expressed subject. The ASV supplies '[the angel]', and the LXX reads a relative clause, 'to the Lord who works wonders'; the line leaves the subject unexpressed (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`; `peli-wonderful-name-judges-13-18`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ בַעֲל֨וֹת הַלַּ֜הַב מֵעַ֤ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יְמָה וַיַּ֥עַל מַלְאַךְ־יְהוָ֖ה בְּלַ֣הַב הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וּמָנ֤וֹחַ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ֙ רֹאִ֔ים וַיִּפְּל֥וּ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: For it came to pass, when the flame went up from off the altar toward the skies, that the messenger of YHWH went up in the flame of the altar; and Manoach and his wife looked on, and they fell on their faces to the ground.

notes.official: *baʿălôṯ hallahaḇ mēʿal hammizbēaḥ haššāmaymâ* 'when the flame went up from off the altar toward the skies': *šāmayim* with the directional ending, describing the flame's direction, is rendered 'skies' under central `shamayim` (ASV 'toward heaven'). *wayyaʿal malʾaḵ-YHWH bəlahaḇ hammizbēaḥ* 'that the messenger of YHWH went up in the flame of the altar' (ASV 'ascended'): 'went up' keeps the single verb *ʿlh* that runs through vv 19-20 (*wayyaʿal* 'offered up', *baʿălôṯ* 'went up', *wayyaʿal* 'went up'). The central `va-yaal-elohim-divine-ascent-departure` lists this verse among the departures of a divine figure by going up (Gen 17:22; 35:13; cf. 2 Kgs 2:11); the Hebrew does not say where the messenger goes. *wayyippəlû ʿal-pənêhem ʾārṣâ* 'and they fell on their faces to the ground'.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹא־יָ֤סַף עוֹד֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה לְהֵרָאֹ֖ה אֶל־מָנ֣וֹחַ וְאֶל־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ אָ֚ז יָדַ֣ע מָנ֔וֹחַ כִּֽי־מַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: But the messenger of YHWH did not appear again to Manoach or to his wife. Then Manoach knew that he was the messenger of YHWH.

notes.official: *ʾāz yāḏaʿ mānôaḥ kî-malʾaḵ YHWH hûʾ* 'Then Manoach knew that he was the messenger of YHWH': recognition comes with the departure, as for Gid'on (6:22).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר מָנ֛וֹחַ אֶל־אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֣וֹת נָמ֑וּת כִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים רָאִֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: And Manoach said to his wife, "We shall surely die, because we have seen Elohim."

notes.official: *môṯ nāmûṯ* 'We shall surely die' (`mot-tamut`). *kî ʾĕlōhîm rāʾînû* 'because we have seen Elohim': anarthrous *ʾĕlōhîm* in direct speech, without article (clause 2 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`), as genesis-woh renders Gen 32:31 ('I have seen Elohim face to face'). In context Manoach means the messenger he has just recognized (v 21; cf. 6:22); NJPS renders 'a divine being' and the ASV 'God'.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ לוּ֩ חָפֵ֨ץ יְהוָ֤ה לַהֲמִיתֵ֙נוּ֙ לֹֽא־לָקַ֤ח מִיָּדֵ֙נוּ֙ עֹלָ֣ה וּמִנְחָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הֶרְאָ֖נוּ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְכָעֵ֕ת לֹ֥א הִשְׁמִיעָ֖נוּ כָּזֹֽאת׃

i18n.en: But his wife said to him, "If YHWH had wished to kill us, he would not have received a burnt-offering and a meal-offering from our hand, nor would he have shown us all these things, nor would he at this time have let us hear such things as these."

notes.official: *lû ḥāp̄ēṣ YHWH lahămîṯēnû* 'If YHWH had wished to kill us': the wife answers Manoach's fear from what has happened. *ʿōlâ ûminḥâ* 'a burnt-offering and a meal-offering' (`olah-burnt-offering`; `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וַתֵּ֤לֶד הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שִׁמְשׁ֑וֹן וַיִּגְדַּ֣ל הַנַּ֔עַר וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the woman bore a son and called his name Shimshon; and the boy grew, and YHWH blessed him.

notes.official: Shimshon = Samson (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`): *šimšôn* is related to *šemeš* 'sun', and Beit-Shemesh lies near Tzor'ah. *wayḇārăḵēhû YHWH* 'and YHWH blessed him'.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֙חֶל֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה לְפַעֲמ֖וֹ בְּמַחֲנֵה־דָ֑ן בֵּ֥ין צָרְעָ֖ה וּבֵ֥ין אֶשְׁתָּאֹֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And the ruach of YHWH began to move him in Machaneh-Dan, between Tzor'ah and Eshta'ol.

notes.official: *wattāḥel rûaḥ YHWH ləp̄aʿămô* 'And the ruach of YHWH began to move him' (ASV 'the Spirit of Jehovah began to move him'): the noun as at 6:34 (`ruach-yhwh-transliteration-former-prophets`); *pāʿam* 'impel, stir' (BDB), whose noun *paʿam* is a beat or a step, so the verb suggests repeated impulses; the ASV 'move' is kept. Machaneh-Dan = Mahaneh-dan ('camp of Dan', cf. 18:12); Eshta'ol = Eshtaol (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).
